name: The Lounge
_why: The hub of Infinity's map. Four ways out, and WHICH WALL each is in is decided by the map in story.js — see the diagram on ROOMS.lounge — not by whatever the generator felt like drawing.
summary: A warm, crowded tavern lounge in a magical realm, in dark blue-grey brick above dark timber wainscot with one continuous rail running the full width of the back wall at the same height all the way across, lit by candles and lanterns.
floor: warm honey-brown wooden plank floorboards, many narrow boards running left to right with staggered end joints, visible grain, knots and scuffed wear
_wall_why: A floor-plate room ships ONLY its floor, so the room's own back wall is a PROP and has to be generated like one. Leaving it out of the spec is how the lab ended up with its jar shelf repeated three times across the wall — there was no plain panel to put either side of it.
wall: a wide upright rectangular slab of dark blue-grey brick wall above dark timber wainscot with a continuous moulded rail between them, a small lit lantern on it, and NOTHING else — no shelf, no door, no opening

doors.look: ONE open arched stone doorway, empty and warmly lit from beyond

contains: a long wooden BAR COUNTER standing along the RIGHT-HAND END of the back wall, with a tall shelf of coloured bottles behind it
two small round wooden tables with stools, off to the LEFT on the open floor
_wallSeam_why: 72, which is where this room's own wall panels are grounded in story.js. It was briefly recorded as 47: that number came from running room.py wallseam against art-src/lounge_scene.png, and the composed SCENE is a different picture from the shipped room — it is generated to be MEASURED for prop sizes, never to be shipped, and its wall line does not land where the assembled room's does. room.py verify caught the disagreement immediately by comparing the seam against the wall panels' declared y. Measure the seam on what ships.
